description: Managing IT projects through all ten knowledge areas, from charter to closure, with the quantitative tools of scheduling, cost and risk and the agile practices that modern software teams use. Taught to the depth of the professional project management body of knowledge.
modelledOn: PMI, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK, 6th and 7th editions)
Scrum Guide and the Agile Practice Guide
outcomes: Explain the project life cycle, process groups and the role of the project manager in an IT organisation.
Write a project charter, scope statement and work breakdown structure for an IT project.
Build a network diagram, compute the critical path and PERT estimates, and resource-level a schedule.
Estimate and control costs with earned value management.
Plan quality, resources, communications and stakeholder engagement for a project.
Identify, analyse and respond to risks quantitatively and qualitatively, and apply agile methods where they fit.

units.title: Project management context and processes
topics: Projects, programmes and portfolios; the triple constraint and beyond
The project life cycle; process groups: initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, closing
Organisational structures, PMO, the project manager's skills; why IT projects fail (Standish, local cases)
Predictive, iterative, incremental, agile and hybrid approaches
Project management software: MS Project, OpenProject, Jira

units.title: Integration management
topics: Business case and benefits; the project charter
The project management plan and subsidiary plans
Directing and managing work; integrated change control; configuration management
Closing a project or phase; lessons learned

units.title: Scope management
topics: Collecting requirements: interviews, workshops, prototypes, user stories
Scope statement; the work breakdown structure and WBS dictionary
Validating and controlling scope; scope creep and gold plating
Product backlogs and scope in agile projects

units.title: Time management: networks, CPM and PERT
topics: Defining and sequencing activities; dependencies, leads and lags; precedence diagrams
Estimating durations: analogous, parametric, three-point, bottom-up
Critical path method: forward and backward pass, float, critical path
PERT: expected durations, variance, probability of meeting a deadline
Gantt charts, milestones, baselines; crashing and fast-tracking; resource levelling
Velocity, sprints and release planning in agile

units.title: Cost management
topics: Cost estimating techniques and accuracy ranges; cost of software (function points, COCOMO in brief)
Budgeting: cost baseline, contingency and management reserves, cash flow
Earned value management: PV, EV, AC, CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC, ETC, TCPI
Worked example: a university management system budget in cedis

units.title: Quality management
topics: Quality planning, assurance and control; cost of quality
Tools: cause-and-effect diagrams, Pareto charts, control charts, checklists, flowcharts
Software quality: reviews, testing, defect metrics; ISO 9001 and CMMI in brief
Definition of done and continuous improvement

units.title: Resource management
topics: Resource planning, responsibility assignment matrix (RACI), organisational charts
Acquiring, developing and managing the team; Tuckman stages, motivation, conflict
Leadership styles and virtual teams
Managing physical resources and procurement in brief: contracts, vendors, outsourcing

units.title: Communications management
topics: Communication planning: who needs what, when, how; the communications matrix
Status reports, dashboards, meetings that work; information distribution
Communication across cultures and with non-technical sponsors
Collaboration tools and documentation

units.title: Risk management
topics: Risk planning; identification techniques: brainstorming, checklists, SWOT, assumptions analysis
Qualitative analysis: probability-impact matrix, risk register
Quantitative analysis: expected monetary value, decision trees, sensitivity, Monte Carlo simulation
Responses: avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept, exploit; contingency plans; monitoring risks
Common IT risks: requirements change, technology, vendors, security, power and connectivity

units.title: Stakeholder management and capstone
topics: Identifying stakeholders; power-interest grids; engagement assessment
Managing expectations, sponsors, users and resistance; change management
Professional responsibility and ethics in project management
Capstone: a full project plan (charter, WBS, schedule, budget, risk register, communications plan) for a real IT project

schedule.title: Projects, life cycles and why they fail
schedule.exercise: Pick a failed public IT project, identify which of the triple constraints broke first, and map its lifecycle onto the five process groups, naming two warning signs missed.

tasks.title: Draw the five process groups as a diagram and place ten given project activities in the correct group
Work a scenario where the sponsor asks for a faster launch at the same budget, choose trade-offs on the triple constraint, and score against the rubric
Diagnose a failing school management system rollout, choosing which causes to investigate first, and score against the failure-analysis rubric

schedule.title: Choosing an approach and tools
schedule.exercise: Recommend predictive, agile or hybrid delivery for three given projects (a payroll upgrade, a mobile-money app, a hospital system) and defend each with project characteristics.

tasks.title: Match six project descriptions to predictive, agile or hybrid approaches and justify each choice in one sentence against the rubric
Enter a 12-task project into the Gantt tool with dates and dependencies, and export the resulting schedule
Advise a client whose requirements keep changing on moving from waterfall to a hybrid approach, weighing cost and risk, and score the decision

schedule.title: Charter, plan and project closure
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page project charter for a farmer-cooperative SMS price service, including objectives, success measures, assumptions and the sponsor's authority.

tasks.title: Select the correct components for a charter in a branching scenario, rejecting items that belong in the plan, and score against the rubric
Handle three change requests through an integrated change control process, approving or rejecting each with its schedule and cost impact
Draw a closure process flow covering acceptance, handover, contract closure and lessons learned for a software project, with owners at each step

schedule.title: Scope and requirements
schedule.exercise: Write ten user stories with acceptance criteria for a clinic appointment app and build a three-level work breakdown structure for the same project.

tasks.title: Build a three-level work breakdown structure for a school website project and check that each work package has a clear deliverable
Interview a simulated stakeholder to gather requirements for a market traders app, choosing questions wisely, and score the coverage achieved
Respond to scope creep requests during a build, accepting or declining each with justification, and compare final cost and schedule outcomes

schedule.title: Activities, estimates and critical path
schedule.exercise: For a 10-activity network with durations, draw the precedence diagram, run forward and backward passes by hand, and state the critical path and total float of each activity.

tasks.title: Draw a precedence diagram from a table of eight activities with predecessors and mark the lead and lag between two of them
Run the critical path method on a 10-activity network, record early and late times and float, and highlight the critical path
Estimate durations for five tasks using analogous, three-point and bottom-up methods and compare the resulting project end dates

schedule.title: PERT, Gantt and agile planning
schedule.exercise: Use PERT three-point estimates to find the probability of finishing a project within 40 days, then show how crashing the critical path shortens it and at what cost.

tasks.title: Draw a Gantt chart for a 12-task website launch with milestones and a baseline, and note the date of the last task
Compute expected duration and variance of each PERT activity and find the probability of finishing within a stated deadline
Forecast release dates for a 120-point backlog from three sprints of velocity data, and show the range with Monte Carlo simulation

schedule.title: Cost, budget and earned value
schedule.exercise: Prepare a cedi budget for a university records system, with contingency and management reserves, and calculate CPI, SPI and EAC at the project's midpoint from given figures.

tasks.title: Calculate PV, EV, AC, CV, SV, CPI and SPI for a project at week 8 from a table and state whether it is over budget and behind
Estimate the effort of a 20-function-point application using a simple COCOMO relationship and give the cost range in cedis
Forecast EAC and TCPI for a project at 40 percent complete under three scenarios and recommend whether to re-baseline

schedule.title: Quality management
schedule.exercise: Create a Pareto chart and a cause-and-effect diagram for a list of defects reported in a student portal's first month, and propose two preventive actions.

tasks.title: Draw a Pareto chart from a table of 80 defects by category and identify the two categories causing most of the problems
Draw a cause-and-effect diagram for slow response in a payroll system with at least five causes across four categories
Plot a control chart of weekly defect counts, identify out-of-control points, and recommend when to act on them or investigate further

schedule.title: Resources, teams and procurement
schedule.exercise: Build a RACI matrix for six deliverables and five roles on a hospital software project, and analyse a team conflict using Tuckman's stages.

tasks.title: Build a RACI matrix for six deliverables and five roles and check that each deliverable has exactly one accountable person
Manage a team in conflict over responsibilities, choosing interventions at each stage, and score the outcome against the team rubric
Choose between three vendor bids and an in-house build using cost, risk and contract type, and defend your choice against the rubric

schedule.title: Communication management
schedule.exercise: Draw up a communications matrix for a project with a sponsor, district officers and users, and write a one-page status report in plain language for a non-technical sponsor.

tasks.title: Build a communications matrix for five stakeholder groups listing information needed, frequency, channel and owner
Choose what to include in a weekly status report from the project data and the audience, and score the clarity against the rubric
Deliver bad news about a delayed launch to a sponsor in a branching scenario, choosing wording and options, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Risk identification and analysis
schedule.exercise: Build a risk register with ten risks for a mobile banking app, score probability and impact, rank them, and compute the expected monetary value for the top three.

tasks.title: Score eight risks for probability and impact, place them in a matrix, and list the three highest ranked in a risk register
Compute expected monetary values for two decision tree branches on build versus buy and recommend the option with the better expected value
Run a Monte Carlo simulation of a 6-task schedule with triangular durations and report the 80 percent confidence completion date

schedule.title: Risk responses and common IT risks
schedule.exercise: For five common IT risks including load-shedding and poor connectivity, choose a response strategy, define a trigger and a contingency plan, and name an owner.

tasks.title: Select avoid, mitigate, transfer or accept for six risks in a scenario and justify each choice against the rubric
Add risk response tasks into a Gantt chart for a data-centre project, including a generator backup, and recheck the schedule impact
Manage a project through a vendor failure, a power outage and a requirements change, balancing reserves, and compare final outcomes

schedule.title: Stakeholders, ethics and capstone planning
schedule.exercise: Complete and present a project plan pack for a real IT project, including charter, WBS, schedule, budget, risk register and communications plan, with a note on ethical duties.

tasks.title: Place twelve stakeholders on a power-interest grid and list the engagement approach for each quadrant
Respond to a request from a manager to hide a security flaw before launch, choosing actions, and score against the ethics rubric
Produce a WBS, precedence network with critical path, and Gantt chart for a capstone project and check all three agree on dates
